transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably nothing major, honestly. But... I guess I came in because for the last few weeks, I’ve just barely had an appetite. 

Usually, after a long shift watching the monitors, I look forward to grabbing something I like. But lately, even my favorite foods just kind of... sit there. I end up having to just force down a few bites. Does that make sense? I just thought maybe I should get it checked out, if that was the right thing to do.
Have you noticed any weight loss or other changes in your body since your appetite decreased?

Um, no, not really. I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently or anything, so I couldn't give you an exact number. But my work uniform still fits pretty much exactly the same, so I don't think I've lost any weight. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, I'm really not trying to make a big deal out of nothing if it's just a normal phase people go through. But yeah, no major changes to my body that I've noticed. I probably should have weighed myself before coming in so I could give you a better answer, I'm sorry. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything. I know a lot of people have it way worse, so I really try to just push through it. 

But I guess, yeah, I have been feeling a little... off. Not really crying-sad, but... most days I feel like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around. It's hard to explain. Like, even when I’m home with my family, or just sitting in the break room at work, I’m just not really there. 

I try my best to put on a good face for everyone, though, so I don't bring them down. I'm sure it's probably just a normal funk, right? I hope that doesn't sound too weird. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

Um, well, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound lazy or anything. I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies. But... yeah, I used to really look forward to my morning runs, you know? And I’d play my guitar a bit, or cook a nice dinner for the family. 

Lately, though... I don't know, I just keep skipping them. It’s not that I don't want to be active or helpful, it's just... they kind of feel like chores right now. Like I just can't quite get myself to care about doing them the way I used to. I feel terrible about it, honestly, especially the cooking. I should be doing more. Does that make sense, though? Like, is it normal to just kind of lose steam like that for a while?
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past few weeks?

Um, yeah... I guess it kind of goes back to what I was saying a minute ago? About that... that heavy, flat feeling? I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself. But yeah, it’s been pretty much every day for the last couple of weeks. Almost the whole day, too. 

Whether I'm watching the security monitors at work or sitting at home with the family, it's just... there. Like I'm just going through the motions and not really present. I really try to snap out of it, you know? I don't want to be a downer or a burden on anyone, so I try to just smile and do my job. 

I feel a little guilty even admitting it's been going on this long, honestly. I feel like I should be able to just push past it on my own by now. Does that... does that make sense, doctor? Am I giving you the right kind of details?
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even if you're not doing much?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm, like, exhausted or anything. I don't want you to think I'm slacking off at work or just laying around all day. I definitely still make sure I get my shifts done and help out around the house. 

But I guess... maybe I've been a little more tired than usual? It's not like I'm doing any heavy lifting—my job is mostly just watching the monitors, so it's not physically hard. But even so, I just feel a little... drained, I guess? Like I don't have the same amount of energy I usually do. 

I try to just grab an extra cup of coffee and push through, though, so it's really not a big deal. I'm sure everybody gets a little worn out sometimes, right? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for, doctor. I just want to be honest without making it sound worse than it is.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down, or that you're moving more slowly than usual?

Um, well... I mean, I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything like that. I'm definitely still doing my job and everything. But... I guess maybe a little bit? 

I didn't really think much of it, but... some of the guys at work actually mentioned it the other day. During our shift briefings, they said I seem a little slower to respond when they ask me something. Like it takes me an extra second to get the words out, or like my body is just... a step behind everyone else. 

I try to just laugh it off, you know? Tell them I just need more coffee. I really don't want them thinking I can't keep up or that I'm not paying attention. I am paying attention, I promise. It's just... I don't know, maybe my brain is just a little sluggish right now? Is that something that happens? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses for myself.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough, or been overly hard on yourself lately?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I feel like I'm not good enough, exactly. I mean, I know I'm capable of doing my job and taking care of my family. I try really hard to be a good provider and a good employee. 

But... I guess I have been a little hard on myself lately? Just... feeling like I should be doing better, you know? Like I shouldn't be feeling this way, and I should just be able to snap out of it. I feel bad that I'm even sitting here taking up your time when there are people with real problems. 

I just... I don't want to let anyone down. I feel like I'm not firing on all cylinders, and it makes me feel like I'm failing somehow, even though I know I'm still getting everything done. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too whiny or anything. I really am trying my best.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy *any* activities at all anymore, even ones you used to really like?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I don't enjoy *anything* at all. I don't want to sound like I'm completely miserable or just giving up on life, because I'm definitely not. I still try to keep busy and do the things I'm supposed to do.

But... I guess things have felt a little different lately? Like, I used to really look forward to my morning runs, you know? And playing my guitar, or even just cooking dinner in the evenings. They were things I really liked doing. 

Lately, though... I've been skipping them a bit more. I don't know, it's just... they almost feel like chores right now? Like something I have to force myself to do, and I just can't seem to get myself to really care about them the way I used to. 

I try to just tell myself I'm just in a bit of a rut and I'll get back into it soon. I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or ungrateful for the good things I have. Is it normal to go through phases like that, where your hobbies just feel like work? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy *any* activities at all anymore, even ones you used to really like?

Oh, um, I'm sorry, did I not explain that right a second ago? I hope I didn't confuse you. 

But, um, yeah, like I was saying, I definitely don't want you to think I've completely lost interest in everything. I really don't feel that way. I still enjoy stuff. Like, watching a game on my days off, or just hanging out... I can still get a kick out of that. It's definitely not like I don't enjoy *any* activities at all. I try really hard to stay positive and keep doing normal things, you know? 

Did... did I answer that better this time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed that most activities you used to enjoy feel completely uninteresting or meaningless to you now?

Um, well, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much here, I really don't want to waste your time. But, um... I wouldn't say they feel completely meaningless. That sounds so harsh, you know? I definitely don't want to come across as someone who just doesn't care about anything. 

It's more just... like I mentioned before, things like my morning runs or playing my guitar, even just cooking a nice dinner... I used to really look forward to those. But lately, I've just been skipping them. It's embarrassing to admit, but they just feel like chores right now. I just can't seem to get myself to care about them the way I used to, even though I know I should. 

I'm really trying to push through it, though. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm giving up or anything. Is it okay that I'm feeling this way about my hobbies right now?
Have you felt like nothing really brings you pleasure or happiness anymore, even things that used to make you feel good?

Um, I feel terrible that we keep circling back to this, I really hope I'm not being difficult or explaining things poorly. I just... I don't want to say that *nothing* brings me happiness, because that sounds so dramatic, and I really try to appreciate the good things in my life. I'm definitely not trying to be a downer.

But, um... yeah, like I was trying to say earlier, the things that used to make me feel really good... they just aren't doing it right now. My morning runs, picking up the guitar, cooking a nice meal... I used to genuinely love doing those things. But lately, I just keep skipping them. I hate to admit it, but they just feel like chores that I can't seem to make myself care about. 

I'm really trying my best to snap out of it, though. I know I just need to try harder. Does that answer your question better? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, like your hobbies or time with family, don’t bring you any pleasure at all anymore?

Oh, wow, I am so sorry. I feel like I'm really making your job difficult today by making you ask the same thing over and over. I promise I'm not trying to be evasive or anything, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

I just... I really don't want to sound like this terrible guy who doesn't care about his family or his life, you know? I still love my family, I really do. But, um... as far as my hobbies go, yeah, it's just like I was trying to explain before. I used to genuinely look forward to my morning runs, and playing my guitar, and cooking dinner. But lately, I just keep skipping all of it. I feel so guilty even saying it out loud because it sounds so lazy, but they really do just feel like chores right now. I just can't seem to get myself to care about doing them. 

I'm so sorry if I keep messing up the answer. Did I finally explain that the way you needed me to?
Would you say that you've felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past 2 weeks?

Um, I really hope I'm not complaining too much... I know people have it a lot worse than I do, and I'm honestly trying to just push through it. I don't want to sound like I'm just whining or feeling sorry for myself. 

But, um... yeah, I guess for the last couple of weeks, it's been pretty constant. I wouldn't call it like, a deep, dark depression or anything scary like that. It's more just... most days I feel like I'm carrying this heavy, flat feeling around. Even when I'm home with my family, or just sitting in the break room at work, it's like I'm just not really there. I'm just kind of going through the motions. 

I'm really trying to snap out of it, though, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting by describing it that way.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in all the things you used to enjoy, like even the smallest pleasures or hobbies that used to make you happy?

Oh, geez, I am so sorry. I feel awful that we're still stuck on this, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you. I feel like I'm just not giving you the clear yes or no that you need, and I really apologize for that. I'm trying my best to be helpful, I promise.

I just... saying I've "completely lost interest" in *all* things just sounds so extreme, you know? Like I'm totally giving up, and I really don't want you to think I'm that kind of person. I'm still trying. But, um... yeah, to be completely honest, it's just like I was saying a minute ago. The things I used to really like doing—my morning runs, strumming the guitar, making a nice dinner—I just keep skipping them. I know I should do them, but they just feel like chores right now, and I can't seem to muster up the energy to care. 

I'm really sorry to keep repeating myself. I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not being too difficult.
Would you say that *nothing* you do brings you any enjoyment anymore, even things you used to really like or even small, simple pleasures?

Oh, wow, I'm... I'm so sorry. I feel like I'm making you go in circles, and I really don't mean to be difficult. I know you're just trying to get a clear picture, and I'm probably not being very helpful by overcomplicating it. 

I just... I guess the word "nothing" just sounds so harsh, like I'm completely broken or something. I really want to be the kind of guy who can still find the silver lining, you know? But... if I'm being totally honest, and I know I've said this a few times now... it's just that the stuff I used to really enjoy, like getting out for a run before work, or picking up my guitar, or even just making a nice meal... I just don't have the drive for it. I keep putting it all off because it just feels like extra work, and I can't seem to find that spark of enjoyment in it anymore. 

I'm really trying, though. I hope that makes sense? I'm so sorry if I'm just repeating the same thing again. Did that answer it a little better?
Would you say that you feel no interest or pleasure in *almost everything* you do now, even things you used to really enjoy?

I know, I know, we keep coming back to this, and I am so sorry I'm not giving you the exact answer you're looking for. I feel terrible that I'm making this harder than it needs to be. I really don't want you to think I'm just shutting down on you or being uncooperative.

It's just... saying "almost everything" still makes me feel like I'm failing somehow, like I'm just letting everything go. But... yeah, I guess if I look at it objectively, it's exactly what I've been saying. The things that used to be my outlets—you know, lacing up my shoes for a run, sitting down with the guitar, or even just taking the time to cook a decent dinner—I'm just not doing them. I look at them and just think, "Why bother?" They just feel like obligations now, like chores I just don't have the energy for. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm sounding like a broken record. I really hope I'm making sense and giving you what you need to know. Am I doing okay?
Would you say that you feel no interest or pleasure in almost everything you do now, even things you used to really enjoy?

Oh, gosh, I am so sorry... did I misunderstand the question before? I feel terrible if I'm making you repeat yourself. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer, and I hate thinking I'm being difficult. 

Um... yes, I guess the answer is yes. It's just hard to admit because I don't want to sound lazy or like I'm not trying, you know? But... just like I was saying about my morning runs, or playing my guitar, or cooking a nice dinner... I really used to look forward to those things. They were the best parts of my day. But lately, I just keep skipping them. They honestly just feel like chores now, and I just can't get myself to care about doing them. 

I really am trying to push through it, though, I promise. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I did a better job answering this time.
Have your feelings of low mood and loss of interest started to seriously interfere with your ability to do your job or take care of your usual responsibilities at home?

Oh, um... I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm completely falling apart or anything. I promise I'm still showing up for my shifts and getting the basics done around the house. I really try to be reliable, you know? I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off.

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I know you need me to be honest—it has been a little tougher lately. I work surveillance, and... I did make a couple of documentation mistakes recently. And there was one time I missed a cue on the monitors. My supervisor had to give me a formal warning. I felt awful about it, I really did. It's just... it's not like me at all. I usually pride myself on catching everything. 

So, I guess it is starting to affect things a little bit, even though I'm really trying hard not to let it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too incompetent... I really am trying to keep it all together.
